q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of synthetic rope per kg?
title: Synthetic rope carbon footprint per kg
short: A synthetic rope is mostly polymer: multiply the resin or yarn per kg of rope by your supplier's per-kg figure. Add extrusion, twisting and braiding electricity and packing, then divide the plant's energy by kg of rope dispatched.
audience: Polypropylene, nylon and polyester rope makers

ul: Polypropylene, nylon or polyester granules or yarn by weight.

p: Report per kg of rope by polymer. Recycled granules usually carry a lower per-kg figure than virgin resin, so name the source.

example.title: Worked example: synthetic rope unit per kg (one month)
lines: Plant total: 42,600 / 80,000 = 0.532 kg CO2 per kg
Add polymer and packing for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
